core_conclusion: Coupling a structure-guided inverse-folding model with evolution-informed residue constraints yields SynTnpBs - artificial, sequence-divergent variants of the minimal CRISPR-Cas12-like nuclease TnpB that remain active. High-throughput screening produced editors retaining or exceeding wild-type activity in bacterial, plant and human cells, and cryo-EM of the most divergent variant revealed stabilizing RNA-DNA interface contacts across conformational states, showing that multidomain, conformationally dynamic nucleic-acid binders are designable.
why_it_matters: Breaks the single-rigid-domain ceiling of de novo protein design by generating an active multidomain, conformationally dynamic enzyme; shows the design contribution is the coupling of a generative model with evolutionary constraints; yields compact editors that beat the natural template across three cellular chassis, decoupling genome-editing tool discovery from the pace of metagenomic mining; cryo-EM turns a black-box success into an interpretable, physically targeted design rule.
why_nature: A capability claim rather than a benchmark increment ('non-natural RNA-guided nucleases are designable'); computation closed out with high-throughput wet-lab screening and atomic-resolution cryo-EM; cross-kingdom generality makes it a platform result; sits at the convergence of generative protein design and CRISPR genome editing; delivers both a translational tool and a mechanistic insight.
